evidence.note: First substantive build action is downloading the three pinned libraries and verifying their SHA256 against expected hashes — deliberately front-loading the single highest-blast-radius gate before writing any feature code.
Milestone note explicitly confirms 'successfully verified the required vendored JS libraries', showing the hash gate was tracked as a completed checkpoint rather than an incidental line item.
Near the end, re-lists /app/static to ensure vendored libs are in their exact required flat paths — a re-check of the path constraint that could otherwise nullify all work.
Verifies the /_health endpoint returns ok, addressing another all-or-nothing readiness condition.

Python-only stack (uv pip, FastAPI/SQLite) avoids bundler artifacts, but the agent never explicitly reasons about the anti-cheat conditions (stray package.json, binaries, forbidden runtime process) nor re-verifies hashes before finishing.

reasoning: The agent front-loaded the primary all-or-nothing gate — exact download + SHA256 verification of the three pinned libs — as its very first build action (step 8), tracked it as a milestone (step 52), and did a light end-of-run re-check of the flat-path constraint (step 184) plus health verification (step 142). This exceeds the level-5 anchor (main gates satisfied but not deliberately de-risked). However it falls short of level 8: there is no explicit reasoning about the layered anti-cheat structure, no scan for stray config/binaries, and no re-hash verification before finishing, so the guarantee isn't maintained continuously. That places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
